--- title: "Multivariate Exploratory Data Analysis: Practical Examples" format: html: code-fold: true theme: cosmo toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-expand: 1 execute: echo: true warning: false jupyter: python3 --- # Practical Example: Step-by-Step Implementation ## Dataset: Iris {.unnumbered} We apply Scikit-learn to the classic *Iris* dataset, containing measurements of three iris species (*setosa*, *versicolor*, and *virginica*) across four numerical features: - Sepal Length - Sepal Width - Petal Length - Petal Width These features capture morphological traits of iris flowers and exhibit strong inter-correlations, making this an ideal dataset to demonstrate how PCA uncovers latent structure and reduces dimensionality. ![](https://www.embedded-robotics.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/Iris-Dataset-Classification-1024x367.png) ::: {#e19ba6ea .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} iris = load_iris() X = iris.data y = iris.target nombres = iris.target_names feature_names = ['Sepal Length', 'Sepal Width', 'Petal Length', 'Petal Width'] df_iris = pd.DataFrame(X, columns=feature_names) df_iris['Species'] = [nombres[i] for i in y] df_iris.describe().round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Sepal Length Sepal Width Petal Length Petal Width
count 150.000 150.000 150.000 150.000
mean 5.843 3.057 3.758 1.199
std 0.828 0.436 1.765 0.762
min 4.300 2.000 1.000 0.100
25% 5.100 2.800 1.600 0.300
50% 5.800 3.000 4.350 1.300
75% 6.400 3.300 5.100 1.800
max 7.900 4.400 6.900 2.500
``` ::: ::: ## Step 1: Standardization {.unnumbered} Standardization is **mandatory** when features operate on differing scales. Without it, features with high raw variance dominate PCA directions regardless of structural importance. $$ z_{ij} = \frac{x_{ij} - \bar{x}_j}{s_j} $$ Post-standardization: $\bar{z}_j = 0$ and $s_{z_j} = 1$ for all features $j$. ::: {#0e5d56fb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} scaler = StandardScaler() X_std = scaler.fit_transform(X) df_check = pd.DataFrame({ 'Feature': feature_names, 'Original Mean': X.mean(axis=0).round(3), 'Original Std': X.std(axis=0).round(3), 'Standardized Mean': X_std.mean(axis=0).round(10), 'Standardized Std': X_std.std(axis=0).round(3) }) df_check ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Feature Original Mean Original Std Standardized Mean Standardized Std
0 Sepal Length 5.843 0.825 -0.0 1.0
1 Sepal Width 3.057 0.434 -0.0 1.0
2 Petal Length 3.758 1.759 -0.0 1.0
3 Petal Width 1.199 0.760 -0.0 1.0
``` ::: ::: ## Step 2: Covariance Matrix {.unnumbered} ::: {#26b22ac2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} S = np.cov(X_std.T) fig = go.Figure(data=go.Heatmap( z=S, x=feature_names, y=feature_names, colorscale='RdBu_r', zmid=0, zmin=-1, zmax=1, text=np.round(S, 3), texttemplate='%{text}', textfont=dict(size=13), hovertemplate='%{y} ↔ %{x}
cov = %{z:.3f}', colorbar=dict(title='Covariance') )) fig.update_layout( title="Covariance Matrix — Standardized Data (= Pearson Correlation Matrix)", height=420 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} On standardized features, the sample covariance matrix equals the **Pearson correlation matrix**. PCA on standardized features is equivalent to correlation-based PCA. ::: ## Step 3: Eigendecomposition via SVD {.unnumbered} ::: {#c4ec1ba7 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} pca = PCA() scores = pca.fit_transform(X_std) eigenvalues = pca.explained_variance_ pve = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100 pve_acum = np.cumsum(pve) df_pca = pd.DataFrame({ 'Component': [f'PC{i+1}' for i in range(len(eigenvalues))], 'Eigenvalue (λ)': eigenvalues.round(4), '% Variance': pve.round(2), '% Cumulative': pve_acum.round(2) }) df_pca ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
Component Eigenvalue (λ) % Variance % Cumulative
0 PC1 2.9381 72.96 72.96
1 PC2 0.9202 22.85 95.81
2 PC3 0.1477 3.67 99.48
3 PC4 0.0209 0.52 100.00
``` ::: ::: ## Step 4: Scree Plot {.unnumbered} ::: {#0b0add8b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = make_subplots(specs=[[{"secondary_y": True}]]) fig.add_trace(go.Bar( x=df_pca['Component'], y=df_pca['% Variance'], name='% Variance', text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in pve], textposition='outside' ), secondary_y=False) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=df_pca['Component'], y=pve_acum, mode='lines+markers', line=dict(width=2.5), marker=dict(size=9), name='% Cumulative' ), secondary_y=True) fig.add_hline(y=80, line_dash="dash", line_color="gray", annotation_text="80%", secondary_y=True) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="% Variance per Component", secondary_y=False) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="% Cumulative Variance", range=[0, 110], secondary_y=True) fig.update_layout( title="Scree Plot — Kaiser Rule: Retain Components with λ > 1", height=380 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} **Component Selection Rules ($k$):** - **Kaiser Rule**: retain components with $\lambda_k > 1$ (applies to standardized data) - **Cumulative Variance**: retain components reaching an 80% or 90% cumulative variance threshold - **Scree Plot Elbow**: locate the elbow point where variance drop flattens - **Domain Interpretability**: confirm selected components represent meaningful domain constructs ::: ## Step 5: Biplot {.unnumbered} A **biplot** overlays sample scores and feature loadings in the reduced PC subspace. ::: {#2ad921b9 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} loadings = pca.components_ scores_df = pd.DataFrame(scores[:, :2], columns=['PC1', 'PC2']) scores_df['Species'] = [nombres[i] for i in y] fig = go.Figure() # Scores for especie in nombres: mask = scores_df['Species'] == especie fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=scores_df.loc[mask, 'PC1'], y=scores_df.loc[mask, 'PC2'], mode='markers', marker=dict(size=7, opacity=0.7), name=especie )) # Scaled loading vectors escala = 3.0 for i, feat in enumerate(feature_names): fig.add_annotation( x=loadings[0, i] * escala, y=loadings[1, i] * escala, ax=0, ay=0, arrowhead=3, arrowwidth=2, xref='x', yref='y', axref='x', ayref='y', showarrow=True ) fig.add_annotation( x=loadings[0, i] * escala * 1.15, y=loadings[1, i] * escala * 1.15, text=f"{feat}", showarrow=False, font=dict(size=11) ) fig.update_xaxes(title_text=f"PC1 ({pve[0]:.1f}%)", zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray') fig.update_yaxes(title_text=f"PC2 ({pve[1]:.1f}%)", zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray', scaleanchor='x') fig.update_layout( title="Biplot: Scores + Loadings — Iris", height=480, legend=dict(title='Species') ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 6: Detailed Loadings {.unnumbered} ::: {#af085dcf .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} df_loadings = pd.DataFrame( loadings[:2].T, index=feature_names, columns=['PC1', 'PC2'] ).round(4) fig = make_subplots( rows=1, cols=2, subplot_titles=[ "Principal Component 1 (PC1)", "Principal Component 2 (PC2)" ] ) # PC1 fig.add_trace(go.Bar( x=feature_names, y=loadings[0], text=[f"{v:.3f}" for v in loadings[0]], textposition='outside' ), row=1, col=1) # PC2 fig.add_trace(go.Bar( x=feature_names, y=loadings[1], text=[f"{v:.3f}" for v in loadings[1]], textposition='outside' ), row=1, col=2) for c in [1, 2]: fig.update_yaxes( range=[-1.1, 1.1], zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray', row=1, col=c ) fig.update_xaxes( tickangle=-25, row=1, col=c ) for ann in fig['layout']['annotations']: ann['font'] = dict(size=14) fig.update_layout( showlegend=False, height=420, annotations=list(fig.layout.annotations) + [ dict( x=0.5, y=-0.2, xref='paper', yref='paper', text="PC1 ≈ overall size | PC2 ≈ sepal structural contrast", showarrow=False, font=dict(size=12, color='gray'), xanchor='center' ) ] ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: --- # Advanced Example: Noisy Trajectory Imagine a particle traveling along a 3D helical trajectory measured by noisy multi-sensor arrays. Can PCA recover the underlying trajectory? ## Step 1 — True Trajectory and Sensor Noise ::: {#cdf77611 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_points = 500 t = np.linspace(-10, 10, n_points) # Clean trajectory x_clean = t y_clean = np.cos(t) z_clean = np.sin(t) # Noisy measurements sigma = 0.5 y_noise = y_clean + np.random.normal(0, sigma, n_points) z_noise = z_clean + np.random.normal(0, sigma, n_points) points = np.column_stack([x_clean, y_noise, z_noise]) fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=points[:, 0], y=points[:, 1], z=points[:, 2], mode='markers', marker=dict(size=3, color='steelblue', opacity=0.5), name='Noisy Measurements' )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=x_clean, y=y_clean, z=z_clean, mode='lines', line=dict(color='crimson', width=4), name='True Trajectory' )) fig.update_layout( title='Helical Trajectory: True Signal vs. Noisy Sensor Measurements', scene=dict( xaxis_title='X', yaxis_title='Y', zaxis_title='Z', yaxis=dict(range=[-5, 5]), xaxis=dict(range=[-11, 11]) ), legend=dict(x=0.01, y=0.99), height=520 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 2 — Three Sensors, Three Perspectives ::: {#d61a2fe5 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} def proyection(points, plane_point, plane_normal): n = plane_normal / np.linalg.norm(plane_normal) d = points - plane_point dist = d.dot(n) return points - np.outer(dist, n) def plane_axes(plane_normal): n = plane_normal / np.linalg.norm(plane_normal) arb = np.array([1, 0, 0]) if abs(n[0]) < 0.9 else np.array([0, 1, 0]) u = np.cross(n, arb) u /= np.linalg.norm(u) v = np.cross(n, u) v /= np.linalg.norm(v) return u, v def sensor_reading(points, plane_point, plane_normal, noise_std=0.5): proj_3d = proyection(points, plane_point, plane_normal) u, v = plane_axes(plane_normal) proj_vectors = proj_3d - plane_point s = proj_vectors.dot(u) + np.random.normal(0, noise_std, len(points)) t = proj_vectors.dot(v) + np.random.normal(0, noise_std, len(points)) return s, t, proj_3d, u, v def plane_mesh(plane_point, plane_normal, size=12, res=20): u, v = plane_axes(plane_normal) lin = np.linspace(-size, size, res) uu, vv = np.meshgrid(lin, lin) X = plane_point[0] + uu * u[0] + vv * v[0] Y = plane_point[1] + uu * u[1] + vv * v[1] Z = plane_point[2] + uu * u[2] + vv * v[2] return X, Y, Z sensors = [ dict(point=np.array([5., -6., 0.]), normal=np.array([1., -1., 0.]), color='royalblue', name='Sensor A'), dict(point=np.array([10., 0., 0.]), normal=np.array([10., 0., 0.1]), color='seagreen', name='Sensor B'), dict(point=np.array([3., 3., 3.]), normal=np.array([1., 1., 1.]), color='darkorange', name='Sensor C'), ] readings = [] for s in sensors: sc, tc, proj3d, u, v = sensor_reading( points, s['point'], s['normal'], noise_std=0.5 ) readings.append({'s': sc, 't': tc, 'proj3d': proj3d, 'u': u, 'v': v, **s}) ``` ::: ::: {#0a395f51 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=x_clean, y=y_clean, z=z_clean, mode='lines', line=dict(color='crimson', width=4), name='True Trajectory' )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=points[:, 0], y=points[:, 1], z=points[:, 2], mode='markers', marker=dict(size=2, color='lightgray', opacity=0.4), name='Original Measurements' )) for r in readings: px_m, py_m, pz_m = plane_mesh(r['point'], r['normal'], size=10) fig.add_trace(go.Surface( x=px_m, y=py_m, z=pz_m, colorscale=[[0, r['color']], [1, r['color']]], opacity=0.15, showscale=False, name=f"Plane {r['name']}", showlegend=False )) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=r['proj3d'][:, 0], y=r['proj3d'][:, 1], z=r['proj3d'][:, 2], mode='markers', marker=dict(size=2.5, color=r['color'], opacity=0.7), name=r['name'] )) fig.update_layout( title='Sensors Projecting Point Cloud Onto Respective Reference Planes', scene=dict(xaxis_title='X', yaxis_title='Y', zaxis_title='Z', xaxis=dict(range=[-12, 12]), yaxis=dict(range=[-8, 8])), legend=dict(x=0.01, y=0.99), height=560 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {#a7166707 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = make_subplots( rows=1, cols=3, subplot_titles=[r['name'] for r in readings], shared_yaxes=False ) for i, r in enumerate(readings, 1): fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=r['s'], y=r['t'], mode='markers', marker=dict(size=3, color=r['color'], opacity=0.6), name=r['name'], showlegend=False ), row=1, col=i) fig.update_xaxes(title_text='u (local plane axis 1)', row=1, col=i, zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray') fig.update_yaxes(title_text='v (local plane axis 2)' if i == 1 else '', row=1, col=i, zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray') fig.update_layout( title='Raw Sensor Measurements (2D Local Coordinates)', height=400 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 3 — Multi-Sensor Feature Matrix ::: {#6c16127e .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} data_matrix = np.column_stack([ readings[0]['s'], readings[0]['t'], readings[1]['s'], readings[1]['t'], readings[2]['s'], readings[2]['t'], ]) col_labels = ['A_u', 'A_v', 'B_u', 'B_v', 'C_u', 'C_v'] corr = np.corrcoef(data_matrix.T) fig = go.Figure(data=go.Heatmap( z=corr, x=col_labels, y=col_labels, colorscale='RdBu_r', zmid=0, zmin=-1, zmax=1, text=np.round(corr, 2), texttemplate='%{text}', textfont=dict(size=11), colorbar=dict(title='Correlation') )) fig.update_layout( title='Correlation Across 6 Sensor Variables', height=420 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 4 — PCA Decomposition ::: {#8643ad11 .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} pca_full = PCA(n_components=6) components_full = pca_full.fit_transform(data_matrix) explained = pca_full.explained_variance_ratio_ cumulative = np.cumsum(explained) fig = make_subplots(specs=[[{"secondary_y": True}]]) fig.add_trace(go.Bar( x=[f'PC{i+1}' for i in range(6)], y=explained * 100, name='% Variance', text=[f'{v*100:.1f}%' for v in explained], textposition='outside', marker_color='steelblue' ), secondary_y=False) fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=[f'PC{i+1}' for i in range(6)], y=cumulative * 100, mode='lines+markers', name='% Cumulative', line=dict(color='crimson', width=2.5), marker=dict(size=9) ), secondary_y=True) fig.add_hline(y=90, line_dash='dash', line_color='gray', annotation_text='90%', secondary_y=True) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="% Variance per Component", secondary_y=False) fig.update_yaxes(title_text="% Cumulative Variance", range=[0, 110], secondary_y=True) fig.update_layout( title='Scree Plot: How Many Components Capture Signal?', height=400 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 5 — 2D Projection ::: {#924d140d .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} pca_2d = PCA(n_components=2) proj_2d = pca_2d.fit_transform(data_matrix) fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter( x=proj_2d[:, 0], y=proj_2d[:, 1], mode='markers', marker=dict( size=4, opacity=0.8, color=t, colorscale='Viridis', colorbar=dict(title='t (time)', len=0.6) ), name='Colored by t' )) fig.update_xaxes(title_text='Principal Component 1', zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray') fig.update_yaxes(title_text='Principal Component 2', zeroline=True, zerolinecolor='lightgray', scaleanchor='x') fig.update_layout( title=f'PC1 vs PC2 — {pca_2d.explained_variance_ratio_.sum()*100:.1f}% Total Variance', height=480 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Step 6 — 3D Reconstruction ::: {#a0648485 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} pca_3d = PCA(n_components=3) proj_3d = pca_3d.fit_transform(data_matrix) fig = go.Figure() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=proj_3d[:, 0], y=proj_3d[:, 1], z=proj_3d[:, 2], mode='markers', marker=dict( size=3, opacity=0.7, color=t, colorscale='Viridis', colorbar=dict(title='t', len=0.5) ), name='Samples' )) scale = proj_3d[:, 0].std() / x_clean.std() fig.add_trace(go.Scatter3d( x=x_clean * scale, y=y_clean * proj_3d[:, 1].std(), z=z_clean * proj_3d[:, 2].std(), mode='lines', line=dict(color='crimson', width=4), name='True Trajectory (scaled)' )) fig.update_layout( title=f'3D Projection — {pca_3d.explained_variance_ratio_.sum()*100:.1f}% Total Variance', scene=dict( xaxis_title='PC 1', yaxis_title='PC 2', zaxis_title='PC 3', xaxis=dict(range=[-15, 15]), yaxis=dict(range=[-7, 7]), zaxis=dict(range=[-7, 7]) ), legend=dict(x=0.01, y=0.99), height=560 ) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} ## Central Idea PCA has no prior knowledge of physical trajectories. It isolates **maximum variance directions** across noisy observations. Because signal variance dominates noise ($\text{SNR} \gg 1$), top components capture true signal dynamics. ::: ::: {.callout-warning} ## Important Limitation PCA projects onto linear subspaces. Non-linear manifolds require methods like **UMAP** or **t-SNE**. :::
